- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., > 2 consecutive negative values), model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +5–8% above true peak.
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive downward moves), model overestimates recovery → reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling, model often ignores sentiment → adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to match sentiment drift.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early period (first 5–7 days) → reduce first 5 forecast values by 3–6% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to average out → use sentiment-weighted smoothing: assign 70% weight to recent sentiment, 30% to historical.
